subject: biology-2
question: A **monophyletic** group includes a common ancestor and all of its descendants. If a group includes the common ancestor of all birds and crocodilians, which set of members would make the group monophyletic?

options.text: Only the most recently evolved lineage, such as birds.
Birds, crocodilians, and every other descendant of that common ancestor.
Birds and crocodilians, without any other living relatives.
Any animal that shares at least one trait with birds or crocodilians.

explanation: Monophyly is an ancestry-based concept, so a clade must contain an ancestor and every lineage descending from it, and no descendant branch can be skipped. A is wrong because it drops the other descendants of the shared ancestor. C is wrong because excluding other descendants makes the group incomplete. D is wrong because membership is judged by ancestry, not by shared traits.
